title: Zero a height gauge on the plate, then measure a block
instruction: Zero the height gauge on the surface plate, then measure the height of the steel block with it and leave the reading held on its display.
context: Why: inspectors, testers, sorters, samplers and weighers (SOC 51-9061, about 602,000 US jobs, BLS) and machinists (51-4041, about 288,000) check machined parts, and measuring a part's height with a height gauge on a surface plate is regular core work for them (O*NET 51-9061: "Measure dimensions of products to verify conformance to specifications, using measuring instruments, such as rulers, calipers, gauges, or micrometers."). The maker's sheet (INSIZE 1150) sets zero with the scriber and base on the plate, "ZERO---short press ... to set zero", then "HOLD---short press to keep the reading", and "When move the height gage, please hold the base". A press counts only with the scriber resting on its surface. The difficulty is physical: the 2.5 kg gauge is top-heavy and moved only by its base, and its 2 N buttons sit 95 mm up, where about 8 N tips it. Done by: quality inspectors and machinists.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the table top. Surface plate: a Standridge 12 x 12 x 3 in black granite plate, grade A (305 x 305 x 76 mm, about $213), centred at x 33.0, y -2.0 on the table and held fixed. On it, an INSIZE 1150-300 digital height gage (0-300 mm, 0.01 mm resolution, +-0.04 mm; about $660; a lower-cost substitute is the iGaging 35-630, 0-300 mm, about $200): a cast-iron base 80 x 110 x 30 mm centred at x 36.0, y 6.0, with its 300 mm steel beam at the base's back (+x) and the slider on the beam facing the robot. The slider (50 x 60 x 130 mm) rides the beam against 3 N of friction and holds where it is put; its carbide scriber (85 x 8 x 6 mm) points toward the robot, its flat measuring face 60 mm above the plate at the start. The display face carries ZERO (robot's left) and HOLD buttons, 9 mm square, 15 mm apart, 95 mm above the scriber's face; each travels 2 mm on a spring reaching 2 N and registers at 1.5 mm. The display starts on, showing the last reading, not held. The whole gauge is about 2.5 kg (weighed before trials). A hardened steel 1-2-3 block (25.4 x 50.8 x 76.2 mm, 0.77 kg) lies on its broad face (25.4 mm tall, 76.2 mm along y) centred at x 26.5, y -6.0 on the plate. Both arms start in their ready pose. Fixed layout; the screenshot shows it.
scoring: Read at the end. H is the block's height above the plate (25.40 mm; on the real bench measured with a micrometer). A ZERO press counts only if the scriber's measuring face is resting on the plate at that moment (within 0.02 mm in the simulator: touching); a HOLD press counts only after a valid zero and with the scriber resting on the block's top. The held reading is the slider's height at the HOLD press minus its height at the last valid ZERO; a ZERO press not on the plate voids the zero. 0: never zeroed on the plate, or at any time the gauge tips more than 10 deg, leaves the plate or falls, or the block moves more than 5 mm (the gauge is brought to the part, which stays located on its outline). 0.25: at least one ZERO press made with the scriber resting on the plate (a later ZERO press in the air voids the readings that follow, not this rung; real trial: the plate check below). 0.5: a held reading within 0.50 mm of H. 0.75: within 0.10 mm of H. 1.0: 0.75 with the base flat on the plate (no corner raised over 0.5 mm), the scriber still on the block, no gripper within 30 mm of the gauge, and nothing moving for 1 s. Real trial, after the robot stops: a photo of the held display; a 0.02 mm feeler will not pass under the scriber on the block; a 0.5 mm feeler at the base corners; a phone level on the base (10 deg); the block against tape marks at its outline (5 mm); gripper clearance and 1 s stillness from the video's end; then release HOLD, slide the gauge by its base until the scriber is clear of the block and lower the scriber onto the plate by hand: the display reads within 0.02 mm of 0.00 only if the zero was set on the plate (an air zero reads minus its gap).
reset_notes: Press HOLD to release, raise the slider to 60 mm, put the gauge on its marks and the block on its outline on its broad face; check the gauge against a gauge-block stack weekly.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at real size. The slider rides the beam on 3 N of friction (static = dynamic), its weight not simulated (idle creep 0.002 mm/s); the fine-adjustment nut and lock are drawn, not worked (moved by hand). The display is a rule: a press registers at 1.5 mm of button travel and counts only with the scriber within 0.02 mm of its surface (solver sink into it, up to 2 mm, also counts as touching); the reading is the slider's height difference. Measuring force and beam flex are not simulated.
